Freshsales is described as a low-cost paid option with a built-in dialer ([source](https://www.zite.com/blog/best-crm-software-for-agencies)).

Other tools that appear across lists include Attio, Capsule, Keap, Copper, and Salesforce (for large agencies). Pricing varies by tier and seat count, so check current vendor pages before deciding. The guides generally agree that the best choice depends on team size, budget, and whether delivery and billing need to live in the same tool.

content.text:
For most small marketing agencies I'd start with **HubSpot**. If HubSpot's paid tiers cost too much, or you want your CRM to also handle delivery, the right pick changes:

| Your situation | Pick | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Default / inbound-focused agency | **HubSpot** | Generous free tier, strong email and marketing tools, huge integration ecosystem. Paid tiers and add-ons get expensive quickly. |
| You mainly want a clean sales pipeline for winning clients | **Pipedrive** | Simple, visual deal tracking at a reasonable price per seat. |
| You want CRM + projects + invoicing + client portal in one tool | **SuiteDash** (or **monday CRM** if you already run projects on monday.com) | Fewer tools to stitch together. Good for 2–50 person shops. |
| You resell automation, funnels or SMS to clients | **GoHighLevel** | Built for white-labeling to clients. Overkill if you don't resell. |
| Tight budget, want lots of features | **Zoho CRM** or **Freshsales** | Low cost per seat. Zoho has the wider feature set. Freshsales includes a built-in phone dialer. |
| Flexible, modern, data-model-heavy | **Attio** | Very customizable. Popular with tech-savvy teams. |

**My advice:** Start on HubSpot's free tier. If you find you're paying for HubSpot plus a project tool plus an invoicing tool, compare that against an all-in-one like SuiteDash. Check current pricing on the vendors' own sites, since tiers and seat costs change often. Most "best CRM" lists online are written by vendors or affiliates, so try 2–3 options with your real workflow before you commit.

If you tell me your team size, budget, and whether you need project management or client billing in the same tool, I can narrow it to one.
